question.text: The equations of the circles, which touch both the axes and the line $4 x+3 y=12$ and have centres in the first quadrant, are

solution.text: Radius $(r)=$ perpendicular distance on line $4 x+3 y=12$ from centre $\Rightarrow \quad r=\frac{|4 r+3 r-12|}{\sqrt{16+9}}$ $\Rightarrow \quad|7 r-12|=5 r$ $\Rightarrow \quad 7 r-12=\pm 5 r$ $\therefore \quad 2 r=12 \Rightarrow r=6$ and $12 r=12 \Rightarrow r=1$ (1) When centre is (1,1) and radius is $1,$ then equation of circle is $$ (x-1)^{2}+(y-1)^{2}=1 $$ $\Rightarrow \quad x^{2}+y^{2}-2 x-2 y+1=0$ (ii) When centre is (6,6) and radius is 2 , then equation of circle is $(x-6)^{2}+(y-6)^{2}=36$ $\Rightarrow \quad x^{2}+y^{2}-12 x-12 y+36=0$
